analysis.title: Expedia Group (EXPE) Q3'26 Earnings Review: Solid Earnings Report; B2B Growth & AI Initiatives Remain Key Focus Areas
key_insights: Q3'26 core metrics beat both GS and consensus: gross bookings $34,008mm vs $32,571mm GS and $32,672mm consensus (+4% vs each), revenue $4,938mm (+5% vs GS, +4% vs consensus), adj. EBITDA $1,689mm (+10% vs GS, +9% vs consensus). Results also exceeded company guidance.
Q3 adj. EBITDA margin was 34.2% vs 32.6% GS and 32.8% consensus, 159 bps above GS and 139 bps above consensus.
B2B revenue was $1,708mm, +23% y/y and 6% above both GS and consensus. Management cited growth in the double digits across all regions and now has about 75k partners.
Consumer execution stayed solid: improving loyalty engagement, record attach rates, direct traffic about 2/3 of bookings, and progress on the Vrbo platform.
Management guided to slower Q4 growth than Q3. Causes cited: lapping stronger prior-year B2B partnership benefits, a softer demand environment, and Fall Sale timing shifting into Q3.
Management noted near-term B2B margin pressure as partner growth shifts mix toward higher-tier agreements and as it invests in the one-stop travel shop strategy.
Q4 demand is expected to moderate, citing the US election cycle and geopolitical travel disruption in EMEA.

GS cut Q4'26 estimates: adj. EBITDA to $854mm from $907mm, GAAP EPS to $3.34 from $3.75, adj. EPS to $4.42 from $4.70. Q4 room nights cut to 94.9mm from 98.7mm. Gross bookings raised slightly to $28.19bn from $28.08bn and revenue unchanged at $3.72bn.
GS raised 2027 estimates: gross bookings $140.87bn (from $139.22bn), revenue $17.65bn (from $17.40bn), adj. EBITDA $4.65bn (from $4.53bn), GAAP EPS $20.12 (from $19.01).
GS reiterates Buy and raises the 12-month price target to $320 from $310. Price was $315.88, implying 1.3% upside.

The price target blends 11.0x EV/GAAP EBITDA (unchanged) on NTM+1 year estimates with a modified DCF at 13.0x EV/FCF-SBC (from 14.0x), discounted 3 years at 12%. GS lowered the FCF multiple citing macro uncertainty and geopolitical volatility.
GS scenario values: downside $135 (-53%), base $320, upside $510 (+76%).

Management sees AI as a long-term opportunity for customer acquisition and productivity: natural language search, customer service efficiency, faster product development, and diversification of upper-funnel traffic sources. Investments are expected to be largely self-funded.

market_movers.rationale: GS reiterates Buy and raises the PT from $310 to $320 after a Q3 beat on bookings, revenue and adj. EBITDA. It stays constructive on execution, margin expansion and capital returns despite a softer Q4 outlook.

earnings_insights: EXPE Q3'26 reported 11/4: GAAP EPS $8.42 reported vs $7.90 GS and $8.05 consensus est. Adj. EPS $9.39 reported vs $8.92 GS and $8.83 consensus est.
EXPE Q3'26 reported: revenue $4,938mm vs $4,718mm GS and $4,730mm consensus est. B2C revenue $3,065mm, B2B revenue $1,708mm, other revenue $165mm.
EXPE Q3'26 reported: GAAP EBITDA $1,550mm vs $1,433mm GS and $1,451mm consensus est. Adj. EBITDA $1,689mm vs $1,539mm GS and $1,552mm consensus est.
EXPE Q3'26 reported: room nights 115.7mm vs 112.5mm GS and 111.8mm consensus est. Take rate was 14.5%, in line with both.
GS Q4'26 estimates (new, forecast): gross bookings $28,191mm, revenue $3,721mm, adj. EBITDA $854mm, GAAP EPS $3.34, adj. EPS $4.42.
GS FY2026 estimates (forecast): gross bookings $131,657mm, revenue $16,400mm, adj. EBITDA $4,204mm, GAAP EPS $18.91, adj. EPS $21.46. Prior: revenue $16,176mm, adj. EBITDA $4,107mm, GAAP EPS $18.74.
GS FY2027 estimates (forecast): adj. EPS $24.31 (from $23.29), GAAP EPS $20.12 (from $19.01). FY2028: GAAP EPS $26.01, adj. EPS $30.69.
risk_factors: Slower travel demand from macro headwinds or consumer spending shifting between services and goods could leave bookings and revenue below GS estimates.
Loss of North America share to peers would hurt bookings and revenue and force more marketing spend.
Industry competition could pressure take rates and operating margins.
Disappointing shareholder returns in forward years would remove a potential positive catalyst.
Near-term B2B margin pressure from mix shift to higher-tier partner agreements and investment in the one-stop travel shop strategy.
geopolitical: Geopolitical-related travel disruptions across EMEA are cited as a factor in the Q4 demand moderation.
US election cycle is cited as disrupting travel demand in Q4.

tension_points.bull_case: Temporary factors explain the softer Q4 outlook: election-related demand disruption, geopolitical impact, and B2B promotional activity timing. Q3 beat on bookings, revenue and adj. EBITDA, and GS stays constructive on margin expansion and capital returns.
tension_points.bear_case: The softer Q4 outlook could signal broader travel demand normalization. GS cut Q4 room nights to 94.9mm from 98.7mm and Q4 adj. EBITDA to $854mm from $907mm.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further softening in demand beyond the election and geopolitical effects would indicate broader normalization rather than temporary factors.
